chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿUbaydī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes junub while traveling and finds nothing but snow or frozen water. He said: He is in the position of necessity; he performs tayammum, and I do not regard it proper that he return to this land which endangers his religion.

key_terms.الثَّلْجَ: snow, mentioned as the only available substance in place of water
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which the situation occurs
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, the legal state permitting concession
key_terms.دِينَهُ: his religion, meaning his ability to preserve religious practice
key_terms.مَاءً جَامِدًا: frozen water that cannot be used normally for purification
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum instead of using water
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes in a state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler becomes junub and finds only snow or frozen water?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes junub during travel and cannot access usable liquid water, finding only snow or frozen water. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that such a person is under necessity and should perform tayammum, while also discouraging returning to a place that jeopardizes one's religious practice.
